cues: On a cliff face in Gandaki Province, Gurung honey hunters climb rope ladders to cut combs from the world's largest honey bee, Apis laboriosa.
In spring, when the bees feed on laliguras, our national flower, the honey carries a nerve toxin.
People call it mad honey, and it sells for five times the normal price.
